headline: ‘Breaking Bad’ star Giancarlo Esposito reportedly accepts Islam in Saudi Arabia
summary: The acclaimed American actor recited the Shahada and joined film crew members in prayer during a recent visit to the Kingdom.
details: American actor Giancarlo Esposito, famous for his role as Gus Fring in 'Breaking Bad' and 'Better Call Saul', has reportedly embraced Islam during a stay in Saudi Arabia.
According to Turki Al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, Esposito recited the Shahada and joined a local mosque for prayer with members of his film crew.
The actor's decision was reportedly influenced by his positive experiences in the Kingdom and his interactions with Muslim colleagues during the filming of a new project.
Esposito is currently in the country filming '7 Dogs', a major Saudi-backed action film featuring an international cast including Monica Bellucci and Salman Khan.
The production is part of Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 initiative, which aims to transform the Kingdom into a leading global destination for international film production.
Born in Copenhagen to an Italian father and an African-American mother, Esposito has a distinguished career spanning Broadway, 'The Mandalorian', and 'The Boys'.

headline_marked: 50,000 [[teachers to be recruited]] in primary schools within 3 months
headline: 50,000 teachers to be recruited in primary schools within 3 months
summary: Education Minister Dr. A N M Ehsanul Haq Milon announced the massive recruitment drive to strengthen the primary education sector.
details: Education Minister Dr. A N M Ehsanul Haq Milon announced that the government will initiate the recruitment of 50,000 teachers, including headmasters, for government primary schools within the next three months.
The announcement was made on Monday during the 20th anniversary celebration of Noakhali Science and Technology University (NSTU) and the Deans and Vice-Chancellor's Awards ceremony.
The minister also revealed that the government is working toward allocating 3.5% of the GDP to the education sector in the 2027-28 fiscal year, and 4% in the following year.
Additionally, the minister mentioned that this year's HSC examinations will be held with uniform question papers across nine general education boards.
For Madrasah and Technical Education boards, exams will be held with the same question papers for subjects where the curriculum and content are identical.
caption:
50,000 new teachers are coming to primary schools! 📚

Education Minister Dr. A N M Ehsanul Haq Milon announced that the government will initiate the recruitment of 50,000 teachers, including headmasters, for government primary schools within the next three months.

The announcement was made on Monday during the 20th anniversary celebration of Noakhali Science and Technology University (NSTU) and the Deans and Vice-Chancellor's Awards ceremony.

The minister also revealed that the government is working toward allocating 3.5% of the GDP to the education sector in the 2027-28 fiscal year, and 4% in the following year.

Additionally, the minister mentioned that this year's HSC examinations will be held with uniform question papers across nine general education boards.

For Madrasah and Technical Education boards, exams will be held with the same question papers for subjects where the curriculum and content are identical.
